sources.title: Buying Platinum, Gold, and Silver Jewelry
supports: Karat is parts of pure gold out of 24 (18K = 18 parts gold to 6 parts other metal; 14K = 14 to 10)
'Solid gold' means the item is not hollow and carries a karat mark
A karat mark should be accompanied by the name or U.S. registered trademark of the company behind it; if the trademark is missing, don't buy it
Definitions of gold plated, gold filled, gold overlay, rolled gold plate (RGP), gold electroplate, vermeil, gold flashed, gold washed
Check a seller's refund and return policy and get it in writing; search the seller's name with 'complaint' or 'review'

sources.publisher: U.S. Federal Trade Commission / eCFR (National Archives)
sources.title: 16 CFR Part 23 - Guides for the Jewelry, Precious Metals, and Pewter Industries
supports: § 23.3(a): it is deceptive to misrepresent the presence, quantity or karat fineness of gold in a product
§ 23.3(b): examples of misleading 'gold' usage for coated/plated products
§ 23.3(c)(1): a gold-alloy product with a hollow centre must disclose the hollow centre and must not be marked or described as 'solid'
§ 23.18: misrepresentation of weight and 'total weight'
sources.caveat: The eCFR itself states the displayed content is 'authoritative but unofficial'; the official CFR print edition remains the legal reference.

sources.publisher: U.S. Code (Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School) - 15 U.S.C. § 295
sources.title: Standard of fineness of gold articles; deviation
supports: Actual fineness of the assayed part may not be more than 0.003 below the stamped fineness
Actual fineness of the entire article including solder may not be more than 0.007 below the stamped fineness (articles other than watchcases and flatware)
sources.caveat: LII reproduces the U.S. Code; the official text is published by the U.S. House (uscode.house.gov) and GPO.

sources.publisher: U.S. Code (Legal Information Institute) - 15 U.S.C. ch. 8
sources.title: Falsely stamped gold or silver or goods manufactured therefrom (sections 291-300)
supports: There is a federal statutory scheme against falsely stamped gold and silver articles
§ 294 prohibits importation/transport of falsely marked gold or silver ware
